record.scope_note: A Private Members' Bill under the Ten Minute Rule, a procedure that Parliament describes as often a way for members to voice an opinion rather than a serious attempt to pass a bill; included as a pending bill on artificial superintelligence.

verification.note: Refresh of 18 Oct 2026. The record's pages on bills.parliament.uk still refuse the archiver (HTTP 403; the browser retry timed out on 11, 16, 17 and 18 Oct 2026). Stored in this run instead: the UK Parliament Bills API entries for bill 4288 (bill record, stages and publications) and the API's list of bill types, on bills-api.parliament.uk, which was recorded as an official UK Parliament site on 18 Oct 2026 (issue #125). The API is Parliament's own record of the bill, an official register. It confirms the short and long title, the sponsor (Alex Sobel, Labour, Leeds Central and Headingley), the Commons as originating and current house, bill type 5 (Private Members' Bill under the Ten Minute Rule), first reading on 8 Sep 2026 and second reading set for 13 Nov 2026, and that the bill is not an Act, not defeated and not withdrawn. The API lists no publications, so no printed bill or printed bill number exists yet, and it gives the session only as ID 40; 'Bill 4288 (Session 2026-27)' in official_identifier is the database ID with a session the API does not name.
